summary: Yen ta fo is a tangy, lightly sweet noodle soup made pink with fermented soybean paste. For a specific Old Town stop, Nai Uan Yen Ta Fo Ba-teng is a long-running shop near the Giant Swing; its signature bowl adds fish balls, squid, tofu, morning glory, crispy wonton and other toppings. The broth and some toppings include seafood and pork, so confirm ingredients directly if you have dietary restrictions.
whyGo: Try one of Bangkok’s distinctive noodle soups in its characteristic pink broth.
Nai Uan’s official menu lists a broad topping mix and several noodle choices, including wide rice noodles.
The Sao Chingcha branch makes a handy meal stop while exploring the Giant Swing and Old Town.
bestFor: Curious eaters who enjoy savory, tangy soups and fish-ball or seafood toppings.
A quick casual lunch in the Phra Nakhon area.
skipIf: You avoid seafood, pork, fish sauce or fermented soybean products and need a guaranteed separate preparation.
You require step-free access or a confirmed accessible toilet; these details are not published.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes for a meal; this is a planning estimate, with extra time possible if the shop is busy.
cost: The official menu lists dishes but no prices. Set aside roughly ฿60–120 per bowl as a planning allowance; confirm current prices and payment options at the shop.
hours: Official listing: Monday–Friday 09:00–20:00; Saturday–Sunday 09:00–16:00. Closed on the last Sunday of each month. Holiday changes are not posted for December 2026.
bestTime: Go before the lunch rush or early in the day. Choose a weekday for the longest published opening window, and avoid the last Sunday of the month.
gettingThere: The branch is at 41 Nava Road, Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon, near the Giant Swing. A taxi or local bus is practical; it is a few hundred metres from the Giant Swing. Walking time from other Old Town sights varies.
booking: No table-booking process is published. For a group or a holiday visit, call ahead at +66 91 541 3875 to check opening and seating.
accessibility: Accessibility details are not published. The original branch is described as a small shop, with some seating extending across the lane; step-free entry, accessible toilet and seating dimensions are unverified.
practicalTips: Order hot soup or the dry version; the official menu also lists five noodle choices, including wide rice noodles and egg noodles.

The named signature bowl includes ba-teng pork, pork blood, squid, fish balls, fried shrimp balls, tofu, morning glory and crispy wonton. Ask for a clear-soup fish-ball noodle dish if you prefer to avoid the pink sauce, then verify ingredients.
Expect a casual, busy noodle-shop setting. Keep the address in Thai handy: นายอ้วนเย็นตาโฟ เสาชิงช้า, 41 ซอยนาวา.
decemberNotes: December is a comfortable time to combine lunch with an Old Town walk, but no special seasonal menu or event is advertised. December 2026 holiday hours are not yet confirmed; the listed Sunday schedule is short and the last Sunday each month is closed, so check the official page or phone before making a dedicated trip.
uncertainties: Current bowl prices, payment methods, queue length and any December 2026 holiday closures are unverified.
Step-free access and dietary cross-contact arrangements are not documented.
The reference photograph is from a food writer’s visit and is not verified as the exact current presentation or a recent image of the branch.
